chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Wahb ibn Hafss from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Badaenah (year-old camel) and the cow suffice for seven people if they gather from one household and from others.

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةُ: A female camel of a specific age (usually 5 years) used for sacrifice

ai.seo_question: How many people can share one cow or camel for Qurbani according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the flexibility of Qurbani participation, affirming that a single Badaenah (five-year-old camel) or cow suffices for seven people regardless of their familial relationship. This ruling underscores the communal nature of the sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence, allowing both family members and unrelated individuals to share the reward and meat. It reflects the practical application of Quranic injunctions on sacrifice, emphasizing accessibility and shared spiritual benefit.
